title: Beyond growth limitation: rethinking carbon dynamics at the alpine treeline. A commentary on ‘The role of elevation, tree height and crown position on the carbon balance of trees at the southern Andes treeline’
content: Alpine treelines, the upper elevation limit of tree growth, have captivated attention for hundreds of years. They are conspicuous and enigmatic. Despite >100 years of scientific research dedicated to discerning the mechanisms of causation of these ecotones, the causes (and consequences) of these ecotones are still debated to this day. Although alpine treeline systems occur worldwide, a universal agreement of the ecophysiological causes of treelines is still lacking. In part, this could be because many studies investigating organismal ecophysiology at alpine treeline ecotones have been conducted on trees in the Pinus family in the Northern Hemisphere (one exception is the study by Ball et al., 1991).
